title: Modales de habilidad, permiso y obligacion

lesson.intro: Los modales anaden un matiz al verbo: puedo, debo, deberia, se permite.... Reglas comunes: van seguidos del verbo en forma base (sin to, salvo ought to / have to / be able to), no llevan -s en 3a persona y forman preguntas por inversion. El error estrella de B1: confundir mustn't (prohibido) con don't have to (no hace falta).

sections.heading: 1 - Habilidad: can / could / be able to
sections.body:
can = habilidad en presente. could = habilidad general en el pasado.

be able to se usa donde can no llega: infinitivo, futuro (will be able to), perfect (have been able to), tras otro verbo (I'd love to be able to...).

Para un exito puntual en el pasado (una vez, con esfuerzo) se usa was/were able to o managed to, no could. En negativo, couldn't si vale para casos puntuales.
examples: You won't be able to park there.
The lift was broken but we managed to carry it upstairs.

sections.heading: 2 - Permiso: can / could / may / be allowed to
sections.body:
Pedir permiso: Can I...? (informal), Could I...? (mas educado), May I...? (formal).

Dar / negar: You can / You can't.

Permiso por norma o regla: be allowed to (Students are allowed to...; You're not allowed to...). En pasado: was/were allowed to. En avisos formales: may not / must not.
examples: Visitors are not allowed to take photos.

sections.heading: 3 - Peticiones y ofrecimientos
sections.body:
Pedir a alguien que haga algo: Can / Could you...?, Would you...?, Would you mind + -ing?

Ofrecer ayuda o sugerir: Shall I...? / Shall we...?

Ofrecer algo: Would you like...?

Todos van seguidos del verbo en forma base (excepto mind + -ing).

sections.heading: 4 - Obligacion: must / have to
sections.body:
Los dos expresan obligacion. Matiz: must suele venir del hablante o de una regla que este considera importante (avisos: Passengers must...). have to suele venir de fuera: una ley, el jefe, las circunstancias.

must no tiene infinitivo, futuro ni pasado: para eso se usa have to / had to / will have to. 3a persona: has to. Preguntas y negativas de have to con do/does/did. Tras must y have to, verbo en forma base.

sections.heading: 5 - mustn't vs don't have to
sections.body:
No significan lo mismo.

  • mustn't = esta PROHIBIDO: You mustn't park here.
  • don't have to / don't need to / needn't = no es necesario, pero puedes si quieres: You don't have to come.

Error tipico de B1: usar mustn't para decir "no hace falta".
examples: You don't have to tell anyone. (pero puedes)
We don't need to book. (hay sitio de sobra)

sections.heading: 6 - Consejo: should / ought to / had better
sections.body:
should / shouldn't + base = consejo o recomendacion general.

ought to + base = casi igual que should, algo mas formal.

had better ('d better) + base = consejo mas fuerte, con idea de consecuencia si no se hace; negativo: 'd better not.

Consejo o reproche sobre el pasado: should have + participio.

sections.heading: 7 - Modales en pasado
sections.body:
• Obligacion pasada: had to (nunca "musted").
  • Habilidad general pasada: could; exito puntual: was/were able to / managed to; fracaso: couldn't.
  • Permiso pasado: was/were allowed to (o could).
  • Ausencia de obligacion en pasado: didn't have to / didn't need to.
  • Consejo / reproche sobre el pasado: should have + participio.

sections.heading: 8 - Elegir el modal correcto
sections.body:
Preguntate que funcion necesitas: habilidad → can/could/be able to; permiso → can/could/may/be allowed to; peticion → can/could/would you; obligacion → must/have to; prohibicion → mustn't/can't/not allowed to; falta de obligacion → don't have to/needn't; consejo → should/ought to/'d better.

Despues elige el tiempo: presente, pasado (had to / could / was allowed to), futuro (will be able to / will have to).

contrast.title: must / mustn't / have to / don't have to

mistakes: NO: You must to go now. -> SI: You must go now.
NO: She musts work. -> SI: She must work. / She has to work.
NO: You mustn't pay; it's free. -> SI: You don't have to pay; it's free.
NO: I can to swim. -> SI: I can swim.
NO: Yesterday I must work late. -> SI: Yesterday I had to work late.
NO: The door was locked but I could open it. -> SI: ... but I managed to open it.
NO: You should to rest. -> SI: You should rest.

questions.prompt: I ___ swim when I was five.
questions.explanation: Habilidad general en el pasado -> could.

questions.prompt: She ___ speak four languages.
Sorry, I ___ come to your party next week.
questions.explanation: Futuro de 'can' -> will/won't be able to.

questions.prompt: When I lived in France, I ___ understand the news.
questions.explanation: Habilidad general en el pasado -> could.

questions.prompt: The box was heavy but I ___ lift it. (un logro puntual)
questions.explanation: Exito puntual con esfuerzo -> was able to (no 'could').

questions.prompt: I've been very busy. I haven't ___ finish the report.
questions.explanation: Perfect de 'can' -> have been able to.

questions.prompt: ___ you swim?
questions.explanation: Pregunta de habilidad: Can + sujeto + base.

questions.prompt: He ___ drive, but he doesn't have a car.
You ___ see the mountains from here on a clear day.
Completa: When she was young she ___ (run) very fast.
'be able to' se usa cuando NO se puede usar 'can', por ejemplo:
options: en infinitivo o con otros tiempos (will, have +)
questions.answer: en infinitivo o con otros tiempos (will, have +)
questions.explanation: can no tiene infinitivo ni participio: se usa be able to.

questions.prompt: I'd love ___ speak Japanese.
The firefighters ___ rescue everyone. (lo lograron)
questions.explanation: Exito concreto en el pasado -> managed to / were able to.

questions.prompt: ___ I use your phone?
___ I ask you a question? (mas educado)
questions.explanation: Could I...? es mas formal / educado que Can I...?

questions.prompt: You ___ park here; it's a private area.
Students ___ use dictionaries in the exam. (permitido por norma)
questions.explanation: Permiso por regla -> be allowed to.

questions.prompt: ___ I come in? (a un profesor)
As a child I ___ watch TV after 9.
questions.explanation: Permiso (negado) en el pasado -> wasn't allowed to.

questions.prompt: Guests ___ smoke inside the hotel.
questions.explanation: Prohibicion por norma -> are not allowed to.

questions.prompt: 'Can I...?' y 'Could I...?' sirven para:
questions.explanation: Ambas piden permiso; Could I...? es mas educada.

questions.prompt: - Could I borrow your pen? - ___
questions.explanation: Se responde concediendo o negando el permiso, no repitiendo 'could'.

questions.prompt: Passengers ___ use mobile phones during take-off.
Is it OK if I ___ the window?
questions.explanation: 'Is it OK if I + presente simple' para pedir permiso.

questions.prompt: You ___ leave early today if you finish your work.
___ you help me, please?
___ I carry your bags? (ofrecimiento)
___ you like some coffee?
questions.explanation: Would you like...? para ofrecer algo.

questions.prompt: ___ you mind opening the door?
questions.explanation: Would you mind + -ing? es una peticion muy educada.

questions.prompt: Would you mind ___ the music down?
___ you pass me the salt? (informal)
questions.explanation: Can you...? para una peticion informal.

questions.prompt: 'Shall I...?' se usa para:
questions.explanation: Shall I / Shall we...? -> ofrecimiento o sugerencia.

questions.prompt: - Would you like to join us? - ___
questions.explanation: Respuesta natural a 'Would you like to...?'.

questions.prompt: ___ we take a break? (sugerencia)
questions.explanation: Shall we...? para sugerir hacer algo juntos.

questions.prompt: Could you possibly ___ me a hand?
Can you ___ me a favour?
Una forma educada de pedir que alguien haga algo:
questions.explanation: Could you / Would you...? suavizan la peticion.

questions.prompt: You ___ wear a seatbelt. It's the law.
I really ___ call my mother - I keep forgetting.
questions.explanation: Obligacion sentida por el hablante -> must.

questions.prompt: She ___ work on Saturdays. (su empresa se lo exige)
___ you ___ wear a uniform?
'must' no tiene infinitivo ni pasado; para eso se usa:
questions.explanation: have to cubre infinitivo, pasado y futuro.

questions.prompt: We ___ be at the airport two hours early.
questions.explanation: Obligacion por las circunstancias -> have to.

questions.prompt: This form ___ be completed in black ink. (aviso)
questions.explanation: En avisos y normas escritas es tipico 'must'.

questions.prompt: Completa: He ___ (have to) retake the exam last year.
Tras 'must' y 'have to', el verbo va en:
I ___ get up at 5 tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Obligacion por las circunstancias -> have to.

questions.prompt: Cual es correcta?
Do you think I ___ apologise? (es necesario?)
In the past, people ___ work much longer hours.
questions.explanation: Obligacion en el pasado -> had to.

questions.prompt: You ___ touch that - it's dangerous!
It's Sunday, so I ___ go to work.
questions.explanation: No es necesario -> don't have to.

questions.prompt: You ___ tell anyone. It's a secret.
We have plenty of time; we ___ hurry.
questions.explanation: No hace falta -> don't have to.

questions.prompt: 'mustn't' significa:
'don't have to' significa:
questions.explanation: don't have to = ausencia de obligacion.

questions.prompt: You ___ bring food; lunch is provided.
questions.explanation: No es necesario -> don't need to.

questions.prompt: Visitors ___ feed the animals. (norma del zoo)
You ___ be 18 to vote, but you ___ vote if you don't want to.
questions.explanation: Requisito (have to) + libertad de no hacerlo (don't have to).

questions.prompt: Relax, you ___ finish it today. Tomorrow is fine.
questions.explanation: No es obligatorio hoy -> don't have to.

questions.prompt: Children ___ play near the road.
I ___ wear glasses now - I had laser surgery.
questions.explanation: Ya no es necesario -> don't have to.

questions.prompt: You look tired. You ___ go to bed.
You ___ smoke so much. It's bad for you.
You ___ to see a doctor about that cough.
It's late. We ___ leave now.
questions.explanation: had better ('d better) + base = consejo fuerte.

questions.prompt: ___ I take an umbrella? (pedir consejo)
Tras 'should' el verbo va en:
You ___ have told me earlier! (reproche por el pasado)
questions.explanation: should have + participio = consejo / reproche sobre el pasado.

questions.prompt: I think the government ___ do more about it.
You'd better ___ late again, or you'll lose your job.
'ought to' significa mas o menos lo mismo que:
questions.explanation: ought to = should, algo mas formal.

questions.prompt: You ___ worry so much; it'll be fine.
questions.explanation: Consejo de no hacer algo -> shouldn't.

questions.prompt: We ___ have booked earlier; now it's full.
If you want to pass, you ___ study every day.
Yesterday I ___ work late.
The puzzle was hard, but I ___ finish it. (lo consegui)
It was dark and we ___ see anything.
questions.explanation: En negativo, couldn't vale para casos puntuales.

questions.prompt: As a child, I ___ eat sweets on Sundays only.
questions.explanation: Permiso en el pasado -> was allowed to.

questions.prompt: You ___ have called! We were so worried.
questions.explanation: should have + participio = reproche sobre el pasado.

questions.prompt: She ___ pass the test, so she was very happy.
In those days women ___ vote.
El pasado de 'have to' es:
Para expresar obligacion en el pasado (en vez de 'must') se usa:
questions.explanation: 'must' no tiene pasado: se usa had to.

questions.prompt: I ___ get up early yesterday because it was a holiday.
questions.explanation: Ausencia de obligacion en el pasado -> didn't have to.

questions.prompt: Luckily, a passer-by ___ help us.
questions.explanation: Ayuda que si ocurrio (puntual) -> was able to.

questions.prompt: We ___ wear a tie at my old school.
This is a library. You ___ talk loudly.
You ___ pay now; you can pay later.
questions.explanation: No es necesario -> don't have to.

questions.prompt: ___ you speak any other languages?
It might be cold. You ___ take a jacket.
Employees ___ arrive by 9:00. (norma de la empresa)
___ I open the window? It's hot.
You ___ worry, everything is under control.
questions.explanation: No hace falta -> needn't (= don't need to).

questions.prompt: When I was 10 I ___ ride a bike without hands.
questions.explanation: Habilidad general en el pasado -> could.

questions.prompt: Passengers ___ not leave bags unattended. (aviso)
___ I speak to the manager, please? (peticion educada)
questions.explanation: Could I...? para una peticion educada.

questions.prompt: ___ we book a table? It might be busy.
You ___ smoke here. It's a hospital.
She's very fit. She ___ run a marathon easily.
